name: Processing triggering and orchestration
summary: How an uploaded capture starts processing: a job status change notifies Antman, Antman picks a route from the project's pipeline configuration, queues the work and submits it to a virtual machine or an Airflow DAG.

roles.note: Triggering is automatic and service-to-service, protected by a shared secret. No customer role takes part. Who may edit pipeline configuration in Antman wasn't traced. Access questions are DEC-059.

actions.action: Start processing for an uploaded capture
actions.note: Automatic on job status change (PROC-REQ-001); no person triggers it in the traced path

actions.action: Edit a project's pipeline configuration and routes
actions.note: Antman configuration API; its access rules were not traced

nfr.statement: Queued pipeline work is drained every five minutes, and each drain submits only as many runs as the DAG or VM capacity allows. The capacity numbers live in Antman settings and were not read.
nfr.open_question: How many captures per hour must the pipeline absorb at peak, and what queue wait is acceptable before processing starts?

nfr.statement: Every capture that is ready for processing starts processing, even when a notification or submission fails.
nfr.open_question: Is exactly-once start a requirement, and how fast must a missed start be detected and repaired (DEC-058)?

requirements.title: A job becoming ready for stitching or processing notifies the pipeline
requirements.statement: When a job's status is written as readyForStitching or readyForProcessing, a capture-api worker sends Antman an event with the job, capture, structure, project, status and capture mode. Other statuses send nothing. The worker reads the job's current state and doesn't compare it with the previous status, so a repeated write sends the event again.

requirements.title: (Current behaviour) The trigger event is dropped after three failed attempts
requirements.statement: The worker tries to deliver each event three times, with a 30-second timeout and growing waits between tries. After the third failure it logs the event and drops it, and still records the event as handled. Nothing replays it, so that capture doesn't start processing until someone notices. A missing receiver URL skips delivery.

requirements.title: Antman accepts the event before saving it, and routes it by status and mode
requirements.statement: Antman checks the shared secret, replies success at once and queues the work in the background. A success reply means only that the event was received. readyForStitching goes to stitching. readyForProcessing is queued only for 360 Image and Phone Image captures, on the configured image DAG. Every other combination is ignored by this path.

requirements.title: The project's pipeline configuration chooses where stitching runs
requirements.statement: Stitching runs on a virtual machine or an Airflow DAG, chosen from the project's pipeline configuration. A route set for the structure wins over the project default, and if both kinds are enabled, the virtual machine wins. A stitching job with no route of its own falls back to a default project's route; with no route at all it is skipped. (Current behaviour) Airflow stitching is then switched to the v9 stitching DAG whatever DAG the route names.

requirements.title: Queued work is de-duplicated and drained by capacity
requirements.statement: Antman won't add a queue row if an active one (pending, dispatched or running) exists for the same run and queue. Every five minutes it drains the queues within DAG and VM capacity, claiming each pending row before submitting it so two drains can't submit the same row.

requirements.title: (Current behaviour) A failed Airflow submission can be recorded as running
requirements.statement: When Airflow rejects a run, the client returns a failure result instead of raising an error. The queue drain doesn't check that result and marks the row running. Only raised errors put the row back to pending. The job then waits as if running, with no DAG run behind it.

requirements.title: The Airflow stitching DAG retries steps and emails on failure
requirements.statement: The inspected stitching DAG downloads the data, stitches, uploads and sends a success email. Download and upload are retried three times; stitching is retried twice and stopped after two hours. A failure in any of them sends a failure email. Each step runs a container image whose tag comes from an Airflow variable.
